newsitem.title: GERMANY: Europe steelmakers plan to grab aerosol can market.
newsitem.headline: Europe steelmakers plan to grab aerosol can market.

text.p: APEAL, the group of European manufacturers of packaging steel, said the use of tinplated steel in aerosol cans should rise to 80 percent in the year 2000 from 70 percent in 1995, taking share from aluminium.
APEAL made the forecast in a statement distributed by the tinplate information centre, its German partner.
APEAL estimates put the share of aluminium cans in the year 2000 at 15 percent, down 10 from 1995, while glass was forecast to maintain a steady five percent in aerosols packaging.
In the U.S., tinplate already has an 80 percent share in the sector.
The statement also said some 8.6 billion aerosol cans were produced worldwide last year, of which Europe accounted for 44 percent, the U.S. for 35 percent and Japan for eight percent.
European output was estimated to rise to 4.88 billion by the year 2000 compared with 3.83 billion in 1995.
APEAL did not provide respective tinplate and aluminium tonnages consumed in the aerosols industry.
Tinplate was being preferred by aerosol producers because of its price stability and technological advances, it said.

These included the new provision of tinplate valve cups instead of plastic ones, which reduced production costs, and moves towards two-piece cans which reduce material input, do not need welding, and can be more easily recycled.
